header.running_head: The Sahabah (RA) Exercise Patience with Illness

blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that fever once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ with the request, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Send me to those people or those of your companions who are most beloved to you." "Go to the Ansaar," Rasulullaah ﷺ said. It then went to them and floored them. The Ansaar then came to Rasulullaah ﷺ pleading, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Fever has afflicted us, so do pray to Allaah to cure us." Rasulullaah ﷺ then prayed and they were cured. A woman then ran behind Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Pray for me as well because I am from the Ansaar. Pray for me as you have prayed for them." Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "What do you prefer? Would you rather have me pray for you and that you be cured or would you rather exercise patience (and remain with the illness) in which case it will be incumbent for you to enter Jannah?" She immediately submitted three times, "No! I swear by Allaah O Rasulullaah ﷺ that I would rather exercise patience." She then added, "By Allaah! I shall never jeopardise His Jannah for anything."[^1]
One of the Sahabah (RA) Patiently Bears with his Fever

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once did not notice someone who regularly attended his gatherings. When Rasulullaah ﷺ asked what the matter was that the person was not to be seen, the Sahabah (RA) informed Rasulullaah ﷺ that the man had been struck down by an intense fever. "Let us go an visit him," Rasulullaah ﷺ said to them. When Rasulullaah ﷺ entered the room, the young man started to cry. "do not cry," Rasulullaah ﷺ consoled him, "because Jibra'eel (AS) has just informed me that fever is my Ummah's share of Jahannam (if they suffer it in this world, they will not be subjected to Jahannam in the Aakhirah, Inshaa Allaah)."[^2]
The Patience of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA)

Hadhrat Abu Safar reports that when some people came to visit Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) during his illness, they said, "O Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ! Should we not summon a physician to see you?" "He has already been to see me," Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) informed them. "And what did he say to you?" they asked. (Referring to Allaah) Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) replied, "He said, 'I do as I please'."[^3]

Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Qurra (RA) narrates that when Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) fell ill, his friends came to visit him. "What is the problem?" they asked. "My sins," he replied. "What do you wish for?" they enquired further. "I wish for Jannah," was his reply. "Should we summon a physician for you?" they asked.
Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.306) has commented on the chain of narrators. Bayhaqi has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.160).
